gloss: no matter what; by all means

definitions.gloss: no matter what; by all means; at any cost
definitions.explanation: Expresses strong determination to achieve something regardless of obstacles or circumstances. Emphasizes the speaker's unwavering resolve.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}が{何|なん}でも{勝|か}ちたい。
examples.english: I want to win no matter what.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}が{何|なん}でも{今日中|きょうじゅう}に{終|お}わらせる。
examples.english: I'll finish it by the end of today no matter what.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{何|なに}が{何|なん}でも{自分|じぶん}の{夢|ゆめ}を{叶|かな}えるつもりだと{言|い}っていた。
examples.english: He said he intended to make his dream come true no matter what.

notes:
USAGE:
Used to express strong resolve or insistence. Often appears before verbs of desire or intention such as ～たい, ～つもりだ, or ～なければならない. Stronger and more emphatic than どうしても.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- どうしても: by all means — similar meaning but slightly less emphatic
- {絶対|ぜったい}に: absolutely — expresses certainty or strong will, but lacks the "regardless of obstacles" nuance
- {是|ぜ}が{非|ひ}でも: at any cost — literary equivalent with similar force
